title: driver-shadowing-heuristics-breadcrumbs
content:
Context:
Quick scratchpad for the odd OOM we saw on a single node (node-g11-prod-07) where jobs fail during kv-cache warmup. Suspect: driver/library shadowing between system drivers and conda/env libs; possibly LD_PRELOAD or mixed libcuda/libnvidia mismatches after a recent kernel update (2026-02-10).

Symptoms observed:
- Multiple processes crash with cudaErrorMemoryAllocation when trying to allocate ~1.2GB for KV cache on batch warmup. Happens reliably only on node-g11-prod-07; other identical hardware nodes fine.
- dmesg around crash time shows: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79" (GPU page fault) intermittently, followed by nv_peer_mem messages.
- nvidia-smi at time of crash reports driver 535.54.03, but LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside the job shows libcuda from /opt/conda/envs/torch/lib (built against 525.xx).
- Containers use our standard runtime with nvidia-container-runtime hook; some jobs set LD_PRELOAD to inject a profiling shim (libprof.so) — suspicious.

Commands / captures I ran (timestamps local):
- ssh node-g11-prod-07; sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-02-11" | grep -i nvml
  -> found repeated "Failed to communicate with NVML" entries around crashes.

- ps aux | grep -E "python|torch" at failure window (captured from host):
  2411 root  /usr/bin/docker ... -e LD_PRELOAD=/opt/prof/libprof.so 

- ldd inside container on /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so:
  libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f...)
  BUT /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 is a shim pointing to /var/lib/nvidia/compat/525/libcuda.so (from older compat bundle).

- readelf -d /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | grep SONAME -> SONAME: libcuda.so.1 (ok)

- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader
  -> 535.54.03

- strings /var/lib/nvidia/compat/525/libcuda.so | head -n 20
  -> shows references to CUDA ABI 12.1 / 525 runtime

- env inside failing pod: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/conda/envs/torch/lib:/usr/local/lib
  This puts the conda lib path first (torch builds often bundle CUDA stubs).

Error snippets captured from Python stderr:
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/cuda/memory.py", line 215, in _malloc
    _raise_memory_error
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.12 GiB (GPU 0; 23.67 GiB total capacity; 22.54 GiB already allocated; 1.12 GiB free)

But nvidia-smi shows only ~6GB used by visible processes at that time. Mismatch suggests a user-space allocator mismatch or a different GPU context.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver/library shadowing: container is picking up a libcuda from an older compat bundle (525) while host driver is 535; results in nvml/nv_peer_mem mismatch and reported memory accounting mismatch in CUDA runtime.
2) LD_PRELOAD profiling shim (libprof.so) is altering behavior of allocations or interfering with memory reporting; maybe regression after shim build changed free hooks.
3) Kernel update changed the nvidia driver installed; compat wrappers are not symlinked correctly, leading to intermittent page faults (Xid 79).
4) Mixed NUMA / MIG or NVLINK config on that node causing incorrect VRAM visibility for some processes (less likely since only this node affected).

Quick reproduction steps attempted: (aim to reproduce in a safe dev container)
- Pull same image used in prod: gcr/redwood/llm-runtime:2026-02-08
- Start container on dev machine with --gpus all and reproduce kv-warmup script. It passed on dev node (driver 535, libcuda path clean).
- On the problematic node, launched a debug container with host /var/lib/nvidia mounted and run: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/conda/envs/torch/lib:/usr/local/lib; python -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')" -> loads the compat 525 lib (unexpected).

Mitigation attempts so far:
- Restarted nvidia-persistenced and kubelet (no lasting effect).
- Removed LD_PRELOAD from a representative job (force restart) -> that job ran longer and did not hit OOM for same workload (promising).
- Replaced /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 symlink to point to 535 library copy on host (temporary test) -> nodes stabilized for ~12h then another crash occurred with slightly different Xid. Reverted symlink to keep host package manager happy.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Rebuild a small test container that prints resolved libcuda paths for all loaded modules and log via /proc/<pid>/maps for the process doing allocation. Make this a pre-run check for jobs that set LD_PRELOAD.
- Ask infra to confirm kernel version & driver packaging changes on 2026-02-10; get apt/dpkg logs for that host (possible partial upgrade left compat libs behind).
- Instrument our runtime to capture both CUDA driver version from nvml (via pynvml.nvmlSystemGetDriverVersion) and runtime's cudaRuntimeGetVersion at process start and emit to job stdout. That will catch mismatches earlier.
- Add a Canary: schedule the kv-warmup job without LD_PRELOAD on node-g11-prod-07 and with, compare.
- Consider adding an admission controller that blocks jobs that set LD_PRELOAD unless they opt in (risky but reduces surface area).

Notes / learning bits:
- CUDA runtime shows allocations per CUDA context. If a shim or incorrectly matched libcuda creates additional contexts or misreports free memory, Python/Torch will think memory is exhausted even when nvidia-smi shows otherwise.
- Xid 79 often correlates to illegal memory access / page fault from GPU and can be caused by driver/kernel ABI mismatch.
- Our previous similar incident (INF-221) was solved by pinning the libnvidia versions in the container; may be applicable here but needs coordination with infra.

Quick checklist to run on suspect node (for oncall):
- sudo apt-get update; grep nvidia /var/log/dpkg.log | tail -n 20
- ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so*; readelf -a $(readlink -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1) | grep -i "CUDA ABI" || strings | head
- check for LD_PRELOAD in pod envs: kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.containers[*].env}' --all-namespaces | grep LD_PRELOAD
- run small repro: python -c "import torch; a=torch.empty((1, 1024, 1024), device='cuda'); print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"

Captured snippets to attach to ticket INF-786:
- nvidia-smi: 535.54.03 (host)
- libcuda found: /var/lib/nvidia/compat/525/libcuda.so (inside container resolved path)
- python runtime OOM trace (see above)
- dmesg excerpt: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus"

Questions for infra / kernel team:
- Any partial rollouts or mixed-driver staging applied to node-g11-prod-07 around 2026-02-10?
- Are we using the nvidia-driver apt packages or distro-provided DKMS build on this fleet?
- Can we standardize a check that host /var/lib/nvidia/compat/* is not accidentally prioritized by containerized LD_LIBRARY_PATH?

Conclusion (working thesis):
Most likely root cause is library shadowing where container sees an older compatibility libcuda (525) while host driver is 535; combined with LD_PRELOAD profiling shim that exposes allocator timing differences -> leads to allocation failures and GPU page faults. Immediate follow-ups: repro container that prints resolved libs, block LD_PRELOAD on prod until we have a safe shim, and coordinate with infra to reconcile compat bundles.

Misc notes (random commands I saved):
- sudo find /var/lib/nvidia -type f -exec md5sum {} \; | sort
- python -c "import ctypes,os; print(os.environ.get('LD_LIBRARY_PATH')); print(ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1'))"
- nvdisasm /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | head -n 40  # just in case

If anyone oncall picks this up: start with removing LD_PRELOAD for a single pod and confirm behaviour. If that work-around succeeds, we can escalate infra rollback of compat bundle.

--- end of note ---
